Subject: Operational retainer model and on-call crediting

Hi Liam —

Thanks again for the call earlier. Per our discussion I've attached a short proposal describing two ways Valence can get guaranteed operational coverage without committing to large up-front hardware spend:

1) Operational retainer (monthly): a pool of response credits + 24/7 escalation path. Credits are consumed by incidents/priority requests and applied against on-call hours.
2) Committed response hours (annual): discounted block of hours with prioritized routing and a rollover window.

High-level pricing is in the PDF (attached). A few notes you asked about on the call:
- Credits can be applied to both hosted and dedicated requests, but there are different 'consumption rates' tied to burst/dedicated capacity.
- We include a standard 4-hour P1 response target for retainer customers; faster SLAs are add-ons.
- Credits generally roll over for a limited period — see proposal.

Can you confirm who on your side owns procurement so we can share a quote and a short addendum? If you'd like, we can also draft language for credit rollover and emergency surcharge.

Attachments: 20270914-retainer-proposal.pdf

Best,
Jonas Weber

Jonas —

Thanks for the quick follow-up and the PDF. A couple questions from our side after a brief review:

- Rollover mechanics: does rollover stack indefinitely or is there an expiry? We prefer credits that carry for at least 6 months.
- Credit decay: do credits depreciate if not used during high-volume months?
- Are credits applied at the same rate for Dedicated bursts or do those consume more credits (you mentioned a multiplier)?
- For procurement: who signs the agreement and do you accept net-60? I looped procurement above.

If helpful, we can do a 15-minute follow-up tomorrow to clarify.

—Liam

Date: Wed, 15 Sep 2027 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Operational retainer model and on-call crediting — Valence questions

Grace / Karthik / Aditya —

Forwarding Valence's questions (below). Key asks we should answer in a single-page summary for procurement: rollover window, credit decay policy, multipliers for dedicated bursts, net-terms stance.

Quick proposal (two options) I'm thinking we can offer:

A) Retainer Core — $12k/mo: includes 120 credits/mo, 4-hour P1, 24/7 escalation channel. Credits rollover up to 6 months. Credits used against hosted at 1x, dedicated bursts at 1.25x. Emergency on-call after-hours surcharge 1.5x.

B) Committed Response — $120k/year: 1,600 hours/year (discounted), 2-hour P1, prioritized routing, credits roll over up to 12 months. Includes a 15% prepayment discount.

Questions for pricing:
- Is 1.25x multiplier for dedicated fair?
- Is 6-month rollover defensible operationally or should we do 3 months with a buy-forward option?
- Net-60 acceptance: Aditya can you weigh in on finance risk / precedent?

I'll draft the one-pager and attach pricing-scenarios.xlsx. Can you give redlines by EOD?

Attachments: pricing-scenarios.xlsx

Thanks,
Jonas
From: grace_oconnor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
To: jonas_weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: aditya_rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 16 Sep 2027 10:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Operational retainer model and on-call crediting — Valence questions

Jonas —

Quick redlines below based on ops and finance input:

- Rollover: 6 months is acceptable if we cap the total rolled amount at 2x the monthly allocation to avoid indefinite accumulation. (e.g., 120 credits/mo => max 240 credits carried).
- Decay: credits do not decay if within rollover window. After 6 months they expire.
- Dedicated multiplier: 1.3x (vs 1.25x) — dedicated bursts require reserved capacity and higher opportunity cost.
- After-hours surcharge: 1.75x for emergency on-call (22:00–06:00 local) rather than 1.5x.
- Discounting: we can offer a 12% discount for a 12-month prepay on the Retainer Core; for the Committed Response option keep the 15% prepay discount but require a minimum 9-month notice for termination.
- Net terms: Aditya, we should avoid blanket Net-60 for new logos; propose Net-30 with finance review for Net-45/Net-60 on a case-by-case basis and an initial deposit of 25% for annual commitments.

Operational addendum to include: credits burnout protection (max 3 emergency uses per quarter before applied case review), escalation SLA matrix, and dedicated-burst capacity disclaimer.

If this looks good I'll draft a short addendum to attach to the quote.

—Grace
Grace O'Connor
Director, Customer Success — Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Operational retainer model and on-call crediting — proposal and next steps

Liam —

Thanks for the questions and for looping procurement. Based on internal feedback here's the short answer and next steps: 

Summary of what we'll include in the formal quote (attached PDF):
- Rollover: credits roll for up to 6 months, capped at 2x monthly allocation.
- Credit decay: no decay during the rollover window; credits expire after 6 months.
- Dedicated multiplier: 1.3x consumption for dedicated burst requests.
- Emergency after-hours surcharge: 1.75x (22:00–06:00).
- Discounts: 12% for 12-month prepay on Retainer Core; 15% for annual Committed Response with 25% initial deposit.
- Net terms: standard Net-30; Net-60 possible post-credit check and with deposit.

Next steps:
1) I've attached the formal quote (valence-docusign-quote-0917.pdf) and a DocuSign link for signature: https://docusign.com/quote/VAL-2027-09-14-01
2) Procurement to confirm billing contact and whether Valence requires any SOC2 evidence (we can provide)
3) If you want a 30-minute walkthrough of the addendum we can schedule Monday.

Would you prefer we incorporate the rollover cap language explicitly into the MSA addendum, or keep it in the quote and reference the MSA? Happy to do either.

Thanks — looking forward to next steps.

Attachments: valence-docusign-quote-0917.pdf

Best,
